summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would update Australia's tax treaty with Switzerland to prevent double taxation and allow information exchange on request.
It would amend the International Tax Agreements Act 1953 to give the new Swiss Convention the force of law in Australia.
The existing agreement with Switzerland entered into force on 13 February 1981.
changes: The bill would give effect to revised obligations under the Swiss Convention.
The bill would add the Swiss Convention to the list of agreements in the International Tax Agreements Act 1953.
The bill would modernise bilateral tax arrangements to eliminate double taxation.
The bill would enable tax authorities to exchange taxpayer information on request to prevent fiscal evasion.
summary.affected: Taxpayers and tax authorities in Australia and Switzerland are affected.

speeches.speaker: Philip Ruddock
speeches.brief: Declared that the Competition and Consumer Amendment (Industry Code Penalties) Bill 2014, the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation Amendment Bill 2014, and the International Tax Agreements Amendment Bill 2014 were referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

speeches.speaker: Peter Hendy
speeches.brief: Supported the International Tax Agreements Amendment Bill 2014, which gives effect to the Australia-Switzerland tax treaty signed on 30 July 2013. Argued that stronger information exchange and G20 cooperation are needed to address tax evasion, base erosion and profit shifting, while supporting trade and investment.

speeches.speaker: Kevin Hogan
speeches.brief: Supported the International Tax Agreements Amendment Bill 2014, saying the revised Australia-Switzerland treaty will reduce taxation barriers, clarify rules and strengthen cooperation against tax evasion. Reported that it will permit information requests from Swiss authorities, including bank information, and argued that global tax evasion requires a global solution.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: Supported the bill implementing the Australia-Switzerland tax treaty and the opposition amendment, arguing that fairer international tax arrangements require closing profit-shifting loopholes. Said Labor reforms worth $1.8 billion had been wound back, costing $700 million and reopening $443 million in loopholes, and urged Australia to show leadership at the G20.

speeches.speaker: Nola Marino
speeches.brief: Supported the bill giving effect to the Australia-Switzerland tax convention, describing its effects on trade, investment, double taxation and taxpayer information exchange. Reported Swiss investment in Australia of AUD $23 billion and AUD $49 billion in 2012, and said access to Swiss bank information would improve tax transparency and enforcement.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: Supported the opposition amendment and the revised Australia-Switzerland tax treaty, emphasising information exchange to address tax evasion. Called for automatic exchange of information, beneficial ownership disclosure and country-by-country reporting, and cited estimates of $7.6 billion in aid cuts, between $21 trillion and $32 trillion hidden in tax havens, and $190 billion to $280 billion in annual tax.

speeches.speaker: John Cobb
speeches.brief: Supported the bill as a measure to update the Australia-Switzerland tax treaty, enable taxpayer information exchange and reduce taxation barriers. Reported Swiss foreign direct investment of A$23 billion and investment of A$49 billion in 2012, and argued that multinational companies should pay tax where profits are generated rather than shifting them to lower-tax jurisdictions.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: Summed up government support for the bill, which gives effect to the revised Australia-Switzerland tax treaty and clarifies 'immovable property'. Said it will enable exchange of taxpayer information, including Swiss bank information, to prevent tax evasion and remove taxation obstacles, while rejecting the opposition amendment; the question was negatived and the original question agreed to.
